overall: The AG found the Ashland Capital Improvement Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of the four allegations, and declined to review two side allegations that did not implicate the law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 4 notice topic 'Bi-law change request from the 3-7 meeting' was too vague and should have named the bylaw and described the changes.
allegations.key_passage: The topic was sufficiently detailed to notify members of the public to that the Committee would be discussing a change to its bylaws.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the March 7 minutes approved on April 4 did not include a list of all documents used at that meeting.
Complainant alleged the Committee discussed the March 23 complaint, a topic not on the April 4 notice, when it discussed scheduling a meeting on that complaint.
allegations.key_passage: It is clear from our review of the April 4 meeting minutes that the chair did not anticipate substantively discussing this issue prior to the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee revoted on the bylaw on April 4 without first responding to his March 23 Open Meeting Law complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee complied with the law's requirements by reviewing the complaint during its April 6 meeting and responding the next day.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the April 6 meeting was scheduled on a date he could not attend.
allegations.key_passage: we note that this is not a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee did not agree on the meeting notice content and that documents used were not part of the 'public record.'
allegations.key_passage: Because these allegations do not implicate the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review them.
